why: Spotify track IDs (22 base62 chars) and YouTube video IDs (11 chars) are opaque and impossible to recall reliably. Never write an ID from memory or pattern-completion. Past runs produced 4/7 dead Spotify IDs and 1/10 dead YouTube IDs because the ID looked plausibly real but was hallucinated.

workflow.name: Source it from a real page
workflow.detail: Not from prior knowledge. Use WebFetch against a Spotify search page, an artist/album page, the YouTube watch page, or a credible third-party listing. Copy the ID out of the actual HTML/URL you fetched. If you cannot retrieve a real page that contains the ID, do not invent one — drop the instance.

workflow.name: Verify with oEmbed before writing
workflow.detail: Run the matching command in Bash and confirm a 200 plus a sensible title.

interpret.200: embeddable. Set verified: true and copy the returned title into verified_title.
interpret.404: the ID does not exist. Drop this instance entirely — do not guess again with a similar ID.
interpret.403: the video exists but the uploader disabled embedding (common for major-label music videos and brand ads). Drop the instance and find an alternative (an official VEVO upload, an artist's own channel, or a different illustrative clip).

workflow.name: Title sanity check
workflow.detail: Compare verified_title against your label. If they refer to clearly different content (different song, artist, film), this is a wrong-ID hit — drop the instance and re-search. Do not paper over the mismatch by editing label to match the wrong track.

workflow.name: Never write an unverified embed
workflow.detail: If verification fails or you skipped it, omit the instance. A blog with 3 working embeds is far better than one with 7 where 4 show 'video unavailable'.
